newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European bunkers gain $1, ARA market active.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers gain $1, ARA market active.

text.p: European bunkers rose moderately on Tuesday, with fuel oil at most ports averaging $1 per tonne more than on Monday, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 cst fuel oil traded between $124 and $125 fob ARA, about $1 up from Monday. Despite the rises, ARA ports managed a large volume of deals, totalling about 25,000 tonnes as a number of end-users either could not wait or believed prices were not about to fall, suppliers said.
"Only one (shipper) decided to wait. The rest are obviously convinced that the prices are going to rise even further," one trader said.
Hamburg fuel oil was steady, but, unlike in ARA ports, suppliers could conclude hardly any deals.
"We're having great difficulty selling anything," one supplier said.
Fuel oil in Mediterranean ports was mostly up by $1 a tonne. Augusta bunkers were up $2, with 380 cst at $130/$132 ex-wharf.
Egyptian and Fujairah bunkers were steady after sharp gains on Monday. Demand was thin.
Durban bunkers also ticked up by about $1. Traders foresaw few imminent supply problems.
